svg.title: Hosted fine-tuning compared with an open-weight model you train
svg.desc: Two panels side by side. Left, hosted fine-tuning service: you upload chat-format JSONL files; the provider trains and serves the model; methods are limited to what the provider offers for that model; little infrastructure work; the tuned model runs only on that platform; offerings change, for example OpenAI's 2026 wind-down. Right, open-weight model you train: you train with TRL or a similar library; any method, including custom losses; you keep the adapter or weights, subject to the license; you run GPUs, serving, and security; portable across clouds and on-premises; more engineering time up front. A green bar underneath says both need the same dataset, evaluation set, and versioning, which are the parts worth owning.

g.text: The provider trains and serves the model
Methods: what the provider offers per model
Little infrastructure work for your team
The tuned model runs only on that platform
You train with TRL or a similar library
You keep the adapter or weights (per license)
You run GPUs, serving, and security
Both need the same dataset, evaluation set, and versioning: the parts worth owning.
Hosted is faster to start; open weights trade more work for control and portability.
